Flowchart for IRS 80/20 Rule With the passage of OBBBA on July 4, 2025, the regulatory environment for domestic content criterion eligibility and LPTs has undergone significant shifts; notably, the requirements for FEOC have tightened. This legislation raises new opportunities and challenges for power infrastructure and puts constraints on developments receiving material assistance from China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran (Martin et al. 2025). For all projects starting construction in the taxable year after 2025, OBBBA will impose restrictions on projects contingent on the level of material assistance they receive from FEOC. Given the significant reliance of the LPT industry on foreign imports, it is possible that the new FEOC requirements will exacerbate existing procurement issues and their eligibility for federal incentives (Kamyans et al. 2025). 20 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3 Conclusion The U.S. hydropower sector is at a critical juncture, with many LPTs approaching or past their design lifetimes, yet replacement cycles are constrained by a globalized supply chain with very limited domestic capacity. Persistent reliance on imports for high-grade GOES, OLTCs, and bushings makes the sector particularly vulnerable to geopolitical shocks, trade restrictions, and commodity price volatility. Regional disparities in pricing are exacerbated by logistics costs, and specialized workforce shortages elevate the risk of delays and overruns in new generation and rehabilitation projects. The current period underscores how fragile the supply chain has become, with long procurement lead times and material bottlenecks coinciding with the need to expand America’s hydropower fleet. While policy tools such as the Domestic Content Bonus under the investment tax credit and production tax credit create important levers for reshoring LPT manufacturing, their effectiveness hinges on parallel investments in upstream inputs, skilled workforce training, and expansion of U.S. assembly
